raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan.

I have 20 mu, wheat-maize rotation like everyone around here in Quzhou. I've done this 10 years. Last year wheat gave me about 480 kg/mu, maize around 600 kg/mu. Not bad, but my neighbor Old Wang got 520 on wheat — he put on a bit more urea at jointing. I might try that.

For wheat, I always use improved seed from the dealer in town — "Jimai 22" type varieties do well here. At planting I spread compound fertilizer 15-15-15, about 50 kg/mu as base. Then topdress urea around jointing in March, maybe 20 kg/mu. That gives me roughly 27 kg N, 7.5 P, 7.5 K per mu. Phosphorus I keep steady — soil here isn't short. I irrigate 4 times: winter water before freeze, then jointing, heading, grain-filling. Well irrigation so I control it. Spray 2 times for aphids and rust, once for weeds — call it 3 applications. Rotary till after maize harvest, quick turnaround.

For summer maize, I plant right after wheat harvest, no tillage, direct seed with hybrid — "Zhengdan 958" or similar, everyone plants hybrid now. Base fertilizer 40 kg/mu compound at sowing, then topdress urea 25 kg at big flare stage. That's about 24 kg N, 6 P, 6 K. Summer rains usually enough, but I irrigate once or twice if dry in July. Spray for corn borer once, maybe armyworm — 2 applications.

20 mu is enough I can afford decent inputs. I'd rather spend a bit extra on fertilizer than lose yield — a bad harvest hurts much worse than 200 yuan extra urea.
